note: The literal launch arguments a build worker is started with, and the runtime seam decision 6 requires. Not a JSON Schema and not under schemas/, for the reason recorded in spec/lifecycle-v1.json. T1 fixes the shape; T3 measures each runtime; T7 writes the driver from this file. Every bound here names the probe in dev/sandbox-probe.py that demonstrates it, and dev/schema-fixture-check.py requires that correspondence in BOTH directions -- a bound whose probe does not exist, and a probe no bound claims, are each a failure. It also compares the LITERAL ARGUMENT specified here against the literal argument that probe ran, in both directions, because matching only the probe's NAME let a bound specify --cpu-shares (a relative weight that bounds nothing on an idle host) under a green 'proved by a distinct probe' (finding 0164896-F1). That is the whole point of the file: a launch argument nobody measured is a sentence, not a bound.

seam.decision: Decided 2026-09-18 by the user; recorded in LOCKED decision 6 and the Q2 row of WORKPLAN-BUNDLES.md.
seam.shape: The launcher selects a runtime and is handed ONE profile object. It does not assemble flags from scattered constants, because a scattered flag is one an operator can drop without the profile changing.
seam.refuse_to_start: A runtime that cannot enforce every required bound in the selected profile MUST refuse to start the worker. It may not start it with the bounds it does have. A seam that silently degrades turns the profile from a description of a state into a description of an intention -- and 'we run rootless' then becomes a sentence nobody has checked in a year.
seam.selectable_rule: A runtime is selectable ONLY when status is 'measured' and its enforces list covers every required bound. Anything else is selectable: false, including the default. Selectable says the measurement exists, not that a production driver may connect: decision 6's gate decides that, after T3/T5 pass. The file says what is true today rather than what is intended.

runc-rootful.measured_on: 2026-09-18; memory swap added and all ten re-run 2026-09-26
runc-rootful.note: What T3(a) actually measured, 9 of 9, and 10 of 10 since the memory swap bound (2026-09-26). It is NOT the shipping default: an escape from a rootful worker lands as host UID 0, and this host has no AppArmor behind that. Recorded as selectable because it is the one runtime whose bounds are demonstrated, and because a file that marks every runtime unselectable would be a file nobody can act on.

no_new_privileges.decided: 2026-09-26 by the user (gate finding t5-e5e3071-F6), after the shipping launch was measured
no_new_privileges.why: rootlesskit's newuidmap needs its file capability to write the worker's uid map, and no-new-privileges disables file capabilities: the worker does not start ('newuidmap: Could not set caps'). The alternatives were measured or weighed and not taken: a single-uid user namespace keeps the flag but cannot unpack alpine (/etc/shadow is gid 42), and dockerd userns-remap is a host-wide daemon change. Build code inside a RUN step never had the flag: BuildKit does not set it on RUN containers (NoNewPrivs 0, measured).
replaced_by: only newuidmap and newgidmap can gain privilege
a RUN's ids map to unprivileged host ids

resolved.repeat the probes in rootless mode: Done in gate finding t5-e5e3071-F6, parts 1-4 (2026-09-26/27): each enforced bound is measured from inside a real RUN step, or on the running worker, under the shipping launch, each with an allow control and a self-test that restarts the worker without the defence -- see proofs. The rootful numbers were not carried over.
resolved.a Delegate= drop-in, or evidence the del: Not needed for this deployment: the worker is rootless BuildKit inside a container started by the platform's Docker daemon, so the cgroup bounds are applied by that daemon to the worker's cgroup, and the RUN-step measurements (cpu 2.0 cores under a 2-core quota, memory killed at 1984 MiB under 2g, fork refused below 512) are the evidence that they reach build code three layers down. A deployment running the worker under a user manager instead would need this again.
resolved.a replacement for the loop-backed quota: Not replaced, and deliberately: the quota volume is attached by the trusted LAUNCHER (dev/quota_volume.py, two one-off privileged setup containers, never shared with the worker), which decision 6 allows the platform's Docker control plane to do. The worker receives the volume, mounted nosuid,nodev, never the device. Measured from a RUN: writes stop with ENOSPC at the quota.

build-worker.description: One disposable worker per build attempt, running a publisher's dependency install and application build. Every argument below is literal and every bound is proved by a named probe.

cpu.enforced_by: cgroup v2 cpu.max, applied by the runtime
cpu.why: A build that spins every core is a denial of service against the content already running on this host, which is the same host.

memory.enforced_by: cgroup v2 memory.max; the kernel OOM-kills an overrun
memory.why: A dependency resolver is the most memory-hungry thing in a build and the easiest to make hungry on purpose.

memory_swap.enforced_by: cgroup v2 memory.swap.max = 0; memory-swap is RAM plus swap, so equal to --memory leaves none
memory_swap.why: Without it --memory is half the bound it reads as: Docker then allows the same amount again in swap. Measured from a RUN step under the shipping worker (t5-e5e3071-F6 part 3): a 2g worker's build code reached 3968 MiB before the OOM kill. Same placeholder as memory, because the value that makes it zero swap is the memory limit itself.

pids.enforced_by: cgroup v2 pids.max; fork blocks at the limit
pids.why: A fork bomb needs no exploit and no privilege.

no_new_privileges.enforced_by: PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS on the worker process and every descendant
no_new_privileges.why: A setuid binary inside a publisher's own base layer is otherwise a privilege escalation the platform handed over itself.

read_only_rootfs.enforced_by: the runtime mounts the container root read-only
read_only_rootfs.why: It is what makes the two writable mounts below the ONLY writable paths, which is what makes their quotas the disk quota rather than one of several.

scratch.enforced_by: tmpfs size=, refusing writes past the cap
scratch.why: Scratch has to exist under a read-only root. noexec is not decoration: /tmp is where a downloaded payload lands.
scratch.measured: The size cap, noexec behaviourally (an executable script in the tmpfs is refused with Permission denied), and all three mount options read back from /proc/mounts. Until 0164896-F1 only the size was measured while the argument specified four options -- three of them unproved, on the bound whose rationale is the sentence above.

workspace.enforced_by: an ext4 filesystem on a sparse loop-backed image, sized at creation
workspace.why: A real quota, and the answer to --storage-opt size being refused on overlay2/extfs. The worker receives the VOLUME and never the device; the privileged setup container that attaches it is the trusted launcher's, not the worker's.

network.enforced_by: a Docker network with no route off-host except the configured egress gateway; `none` is the measured floor
network.why: Q3 set the rule as deny-all except the configured repository hosts. `--network none` is what the probe demonstrates and is the floor the gateway is measured against; the gateway itself is T3's remaining work and is NOT proved by this bound.

seccomp.enforced_by: a seccomp BPF filter applied by the runtime
seccomp.why: With AppArmor unavailable here, seccomp and user namespaces are the confinement. That is a reason to state it precisely, not loosely.
seccomp.measured: Inside the worker, with a negative control: a CONFIGURED profile gives Seccomp: 2 in /proc/self/status and denies a syscall the profile lists, while --security-opt=seccomp=unconfined gives Seccomp: 0 and allows it. Until 0164896-F2 this bound was proved by docker info reporting that the daemon supports seccomp -- a string that does not change when a worker runs wholly unconfined, and exactly the flag-reading isolation test that decision 6 rejects by name.

build-worker.daemon_bounds_note: Bounds buildkitd enforces inside the worker, whatever the runtime, so they are not part of any runtime's enforces list. Passed as launch arguments like the bounds above, and each is proved by a probe in dev/run-bounds-probe.py that floods a real RUN step's output; dev/schema-fixture-check.py requires that correspondence in both directions, with the same argument comparison.

step_log_size.enforced_by: buildkitd clips a step's log once it has streamed this many bytes to the client
step_log_size.why: Decision 6 bounds logs. Build output crosses to the trusted client and on to storage and an admin's browser; a RUN that prints without end must not be able to fill any of them. BuildKit's own default is 2 MiB; pinned here so an upstream default change cannot lift it unnoticed. Clipping keeps the HEAD of the log, while a failed build's error is usually at its TAIL -- what T7/T8 keep and show a publisher is theirs to decide, and this bound is only the ceiling.

step_log_speed.enforced_by: buildkitd clips a step's log once its output exceeds this rate
step_log_speed.why: The size bound alone lets a RUN deliver its whole allowance in one burst; the rate bound is what actually stopped a 16 MiB flood (measured: 235 KB of it reached the client). BuildKit's default, 200 KiB/s, pinned for the same reason as the size.

build-worker.forbidden_rationale: Decision 6 rejects each of these by name or by kind. They are listed literally so that a driver can be checked against the list mechanically rather than read for intent. --device covers the loop device specifically: the worker gets the volume, never the block device backing it.
build-worker.control_transport: The daemon's control endpoint is a unix socket in a volume shared only with the trusted client, not a TCP port (user decision 2026-09-26, gate finding t5-e5e3071-F6, dev/validate-run-attacks.sh). A RUN shares the worker's network, so a TCP port was reachable by build code; a socket in a volume the RUN never mounts is not. T7's driver ships this transport.
never_reaches_the_worker: the Docker socket, by mount or by a worker-callable API proxy
a bind mount of the repository, platform temp directory or home
S3, registry, database or platform credentials of any kind

facts.note: Recorded, and deliberately NOT bounds. dev/sandbox-probe.py records these with kind='fact' and dev/schema-fixture-check.py fails if either is ever cited as a bound's proof. Counting a recorded fact as an enforced bound is finding 7b6e931-F2, and 'AppArmor is not available' is the exact sentence that made an absent capability read as a present one.
facts.apparmor: Unavailable on this host (/sys/module/apparmor/parameters/enabled is not Y). No profile may list AppArmor as confinement; it rests on user namespaces, seccomp and cgroups.
facts.--storage-opt size: Refused outright on overlay2 over extfs, which needs xfs with pquota. This is why the workspace bound is a loop-backed volume and not a storage-opt quota.

invariants: Every bound names a probe that dev/sandbox-probe.py records with kind='bound', and every such probe is claimed by exactly one bound. Neither direction alone is enough: the first lets a probe go unclaimed, the second lets a bound go unproved.

The literal argument a bound specifies must be the literal argument its probe ran, compared flag-first and then option by option, with <placeholder> values matching anything. Lengths must agree, so an option dropped from the profile fails as surely as one the probe never measured.

Every placeholder a bound uses must be DECLARED in that bound's placeholders list, and every declared one must be used. A bare <token> matches any measured token wherever it stands, so an undeclared one can occupy the position a fixed security option held -- replacing noexec with <exec_policy> once read as 'the SAME literal argument' while the probe measured noexec. Declaring them makes widening the configurable surface a visible edit rather than a silent one; the list is required even when empty.

A bound is proved by observing the WORKER, never by reading what the daemon or the host supports. A capability read does not change when the worker runs unconfined, so it cannot distinguish an enforced bound from an absent one.
A name the probe records as kind='fact' may never be a bound's proof.

Every daemon bound names a probe that dev/run-bounds-probe.py records with kind='bound' and the same literal argument, and every such probe is claimed by exactly one daemon bound -- the rules above, against the RUN-step probe. Daemon bounds are enforced by buildkitd whatever the runtime, so no runtime lists them.
No forbidden argument may appear in any bound's or daemon bound's argument.
A runtime is selectable only if it is measured and enforces every bound. The default is not exempt.

Every enforced bound of a measured runtime names its proof: a probe file and the literal name of the check in it that measured the bound UNDER THAT RUNTIME. A runtime cannot borrow another's measurement -- the rootful numbers never counted for rootless, because the enforcing agent changes.
Both runc runtimes are measured (rootful by T3(a), rootless by gate finding t5-e5e3071-F6); the default is rootless. runsc and kata are not.
